dimensions.assessment: The law affects active duty and reserve military personnel, Department of Defense and Department of Energy civilian employees, Coast Guard members, intelligence community personnel, defense contractors, and members of the Lumbee Tribe of North Carolina.
dimensions.evidence: Authorizes appropriations and sets active duty and reserve component personnel strength levels across the Armed Forces.

dimensions.assessment: Effects are major for defense personnel, contractors, and agencies due to wide-ranging changes in acquisition laws, military construction projects, nuclear energy programs, and the granting of federal recognition and associated benefits to the Lumbee Tribe.
dimensions.evidence: Makes the Lumbee Tribe and its members eligible for federal services and benefits for federally recognized tribes, subject to certain conditions and verifications.

dimensions.assessment: The act authorizes extensive appropriations for Department of Defense programs, military construction, Department of Energy national security programs, and various other agencies and defense activities for fiscal year 2026.
dimensions.evidence: Sets forth policies and authorities for FY2026 for Department of Defense programs and activities, military construction, and Department of Energy national security programs.

dimensions.assessment: The scope of change is massive, amending defense acquisition systems, JROC requirements, military construction general provisions, merchant mariner laws, and atomic energy defense activities, while enacting multiple specific acts.
dimensions.evidence: Organizes and codifies atomic energy defense activities into a new subpart B of part VI of subtitle A of title 10, United States Code

dimensions.assessment: While primarily focused on fiscal year 2026 authorizations and appropriations, the act includes permanent structural changes, codifications, federal recognition for an Indian tribe, and multiple provisions with multi-year reporting or termination schedules up to December 31, 2030.
dimensions.evidence: Amends 10 U.S.C. 130i regarding protection of facilities from unmanned aircraft... terminating on December 31, 2030.

missing_information: Exact total dollar amounts for the authorized appropriations are not listed in the provided summary notes.
importance_detail.rationale: This act sets sweeping policies, personnel strengths, authorizations, and appropriations for the Department of Defense, Department of Energy national security programs, Department of State, Intelligence Community, and Coast Guard for fiscal year 2026. It enacts broad reforms across military construction, defense acquisition, procurement, industrial base strengthening, atomic energy defense activities, and maritime safety, alongside specific provisions such as federal recognition for the Lumbee Tribe and various international sanctions.

card.summary: The BUST FENTANYL Act requires the President to annually identify and sanction foreign opioid traffickers through 2030, with a priority on individuals and entities from the People's Republic of China involved in shipping fentanyl, precursors, and manufacturing equipment to countries like Mexico. The bill also expands existing sanctions to cover any foreign persons or foreign government entities and their senior officials who knowingly contribute to or support opioid trafficking or related financial transactions, and mandates several new reports and briefings for Congress regarding drug trafficking and diplomatic efforts.

summary: S. 1071, titled the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026 and designated as Public Law No. 119-60, establishes the policies, authorizations, and funding levels for U.S. national defense programs, military construction, Department of Energy national security programs, intelligence activities, and maritime and Coast Guard operations. The legislation spans eight divisions covering defense acquisitions, authorizations for foreign affairs and intelligence, Coast Guard management and maritime safety reforms, security policies regarding foreign nations and illicit trafficking, and various other administrative matters.

affected_groups.effect: Subject to updated pay, acquisition rules, training programs, housing, and operational policies across all military branches.
affected_groups.group: Military personnel and Department of Defense civilian workers

affected_groups.effect: Subject to new behavioral health requirements, anti-hazing and anti-sexual misconduct mandates, pilot programs for sea duty, and operational rules.
Granted temporary 3-year authorizations and visa exemptions to perform construction, repair, or renovation services connected to military installations on Wake Island.
Gain access to digital resources and training through the newly established Project Spectrum within the Office of Small Business Programs.
Granted federal recognition, eligibility for federal Indian programs, and provisions allowing the federal government to take land into trust.
affected_groups.group: The Lumbee Tribe of North Carolina

key_provisions: Authorizes programs and activities for the Department of Defense, military construction, and Department of Energy national security programs for fiscal year 2026, including funding tables and authorizations such as $531,832,000 for the NATO Security Investment Program.

Authorizes nonimmigrant construction workers on Wake Island for up to 3 years, exempting them from numerical visa limits, and permits aliens admitted to Guam or the Northern Mariana Islands to perform construction labor there through December 31, 2030.

Revises defense acquisition rules, establishes the portfolio acquisition executive role, creates Project Spectrum to assist small businesses, establishes the BOOST program for commercial technology, and creates the Civil Reserve Manufacturing Network.

Authorizes extensive Coast Guard reforms, including a Sea Duty pilot program, civil firefighter incentives, enhanced sexual assault and harassment prevention policies, and merchant mariner credentialing updates.

Reauthorizes and amends laws relating to international security and foreign affairs, including the Defense Production Act through September 30, 2026, the International Development Finance Corporation through December 31, 2031, and provisions targeting synthetic opioid trafficking, nuclear exports, and foreign adversaries.
Enacts the Lumbee Fairness Act, extending federal recognition to the Lumbee Tribe of North Carolina, detailing land-in-trust provisions, and outlining federal service eligibility.
Repeals the 1991 and 2002 Authorizations for Use of Military Force Against Iraq and repeals the Caesar Syria Civilian Protection Act of 2019 subject to certain presidential certifications.

The legislation spans eight divisions covering defense acquisitions, authorizations for foreign affairs and intelligence, Coast Guard management and maritime safety reforms, security policies regarding foreign nations and illicit trafficking, and various other administrative matters.
